title: Transcriptomic profiling reveals macrophage gene signatures associated with lactylation-related pathways in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
authors: Guo, Hui; Sun, Weilin; Zhao, Fang; Yu, Yang; Zhao, Xiaoyun; Sun, Daqiang
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过转录组和机器学习识别COPD巨噬细胞乳酸化相关生物标志物，虽涉及转录因子关联和分子对接，但核心是疾病生物标志物而非蛋白质-DNA互作机制建模，与本课题关联较弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Macrophages contribute to the immune dysregulation observed in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Additionally, lactylation exerts an indirect influence on COPD pathogenesis. However, the specific biomarkers linked to macrophage activation in COPD and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study aimed to identify these biomarkers and elucidate the associated molecular pathways. METHODS: Data were retrieved from public databases. A comprehensive analysis was conducted using weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), immune infiltration analysis, differential expression analysis, correlation studies, machine learning, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and expression level validation to identify macrophage lactylation-related biomarkers in COPD. The nomogram model, Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA), molecular regulatory networks, compound predictions, and molecular docking were employed to further explore the roles of these biomarkers in COPD. Clinical samples were used to validate the expression levels of the identified biomarkers. RESULTS: Three key biomarkers-ALDH2, ASGR2, and CYP1B1-were identified. The nomogram model based on these biomarkers accurately predicted the mortality of patients with COPD. GSEA suggested that the biomarkers are likely involved in metabolic pathways and B-cell receptor signaling. Five transcription factors (TFs), including STAT3, were associated with all identified biomarkers. Eight compounds, including bisphenol A, were linked to multiple biomarkers, with CYP1B1 exhibiting the strongest binding affinity to benzo(a)pyrene. In vitro experiments confirmed the validity of the bioinformatics findings. CONCLUSION: This study identified three biomarkers, offering new perspectives on potential therapeutic targets for COPD.
abstract_zh: 背景：巨噬细胞参与慢性阻塞性肺疾病（COPD）中观察到的免疫失调。此外，乳酰化（lactylation）对COPD发病机制产生间接影响。然而，与COPD中巨噬细胞活化相关的特异性生物标志物及其潜在分子机制仍知之甚少。本研究旨在识别这些生物标志物并阐明相关分子通路。方法：数据从公共数据库获取。采用加权基因共表达网络分析（WGCNA）、免疫浸润分析、差异表达分析、相关性研究、机器学习、受试者工作特征（ROC）分析及表达水平验证进行综合分析，以识别COPD中巨噬细胞乳酰化相关生物标志物。使用列线图模型、基因集富集分析（GSEA）、分子调控网络、化合物预测及分子对接进一步探讨这些生物标志物在COPD中的作用。临床样本用于验证所识别生物标志物的表达水平。结果：识别出三个关键生物标志物——ALDH2、ASGR2和CYP1B1。基于这些生物标志物的列线图模型准确预测了COPD患者的死亡率。GSEA提示这些生物标志物可能参与代谢通路和B细胞受体信号传导。五个转录因子（TFs），包括STAT3，与所有识别的生物标志物相关。八种化合物，包括双酚A，与多个生物标志物相关联，其中CYP1B1对苯并(a)芘表现出最强的结合亲和力。体外实验证实了生物信息学发现的可靠性。结论：本研究识别出三个生物标志物，为COPD的潜在治疗靶点提供了新视角。
